text:
Ethan Moore: quick heads up from today's API workshop. attendees saw the SDK silently truncate a streamed JSON array when using json_mode + schema validation.
Zara Khan: truncate how? like partial array items dropped?
Ethan Moore: yes. model streams: [obj1, obj2, obj3] across frames. if a frame boundary lands inside obj2 and validation fails on obj2 the SDK currently drops the rest of the array and returns the parsed prefix. folks expected an explicit parse error.
Diego Alvarez: that's bad. Do we have an example payload / minimal repro?
Ethan Moore: captured from the console. stream frames arrived as: frame1: "[ {\"id\":1,\"text\":\"a\" }, {\"id\":2,\"text\":\"b\""\nframe2: ", \"meta\": null }, {\"id\":3,\"text\":\"c\" } ]"\nZara Khan: so the validator sees a partial second object and then, upon failing, returns the already-validated first item and marks the call successful?
Ethan Moore: exactly. Debug log: "validation: accepted 1 items, aborted on item 2 at offset 48" but API response looked like success with array length 1 which confused attendees.
Diego Alvarez: this is a UX regression. For structured outputs we should never silently return partial collections; instead return a parse_error with raw_stream attached and make partial parse available only on an explicit opt-in flag.
Zara Khan: agreed. Also worth noting: the JS SDK's default validator behavior differs from Py's historical behavior which raises on any parse issue. Another parity footgun for newcomers.
Ethan Moore: proposed triage: (1) change SDK default for streaming arrays to fail-fast on parse errors, (2) add an opt-in `allow_partial_collections: true` flag, (3) improve error payload to include `raw_stream_fragment` and `parse_offset` for debugging in the bootcamp sample.
Diego Alvarez: add tests that simulate split-object frames and verify SDK raises a JSONParseError with diagnostics. I'll take the SDK change.
Zara Khan: I'll update bootcamp sample and slides to show how to enable `allow_partial_collections` when you intentionally want streaming-first UX, and how to handle `raw_stream_fragment`. Also add a small troubleshooting FAQ: "Why did I only get 1 item?"
Ethan Moore: can we also include a short snippet in the console example to print raw frames when parse errors occur? newbies spent too long copying/pasting.
Zara Khan: snippet to include in sample:
```js
client.on('stream_frame', (frame) => console.log('raw frame:', frame));
try {
  const res = await client.responses.create({ model: 'redwood-chat-1', json_mode: true, arguments_schema: itemsSchema });
} catch (err) {
  if (err.name === 'JSONParseError') console.log('raw fragment', err.raw_fragment);
}
```
Diego Alvarez: filing DEVEX-1501 to track SDK behavior change + tests. Also include a parity note so Py and JS behave the same.
Devex Bot: New issue created: DEVEX-1501 - "Streaming arrays: fail-fast on parse errors; expose raw_fragment and opt-in partial collections" https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/DEVEX-1501 :white_check_mark:
Ethan Moore: thanks. priority for next patch release so trainers don't hit this in public workshops.
Zara Khan: will PR bootcamp updates after SDK patch lands.
Diego Alvarez: ETA: SDK PR + unit tests by EOD tomorrow.
Ethan Moore: great—appreciate the quick turnaround :thumbsup:
